# Quanteda

```{r}
#install.packages("readtext")
library(quanteda)
library(readtext)
library(tidyverse)

```

#Import your article text dataframe
```{r}
articles <- rio::import("articles_df.xlsx") 
```

```{r}
view(articles)
```


```{r}

# Create a corpus using the 'sentence' column as the text field
my_corpus <- corpus(articles, text_field = "sentence") # build a new corpus from the texts
head(my_corpus)


```

## kwic on long covid dataset

```{r}

# Tokenize the corpus
my_tokens <- tokens(my_corpus)

long_covid_kwic_results <- kwic(my_tokens, phrase(c("long COVID", "long covid", "brain fog", "chronic fatigue", "post-exertional malaise", "quality of life", "mental health", "not real", "mystery illness", "lack of evidence", "more research", "disability", "debilitating symptoms")), window = 20) %>% as.data.frame() 

#view results
head(long_covid_kwic_results, 20)

#export results
write.csv(long_covid_kwic_results, "long_covid_kwic.csv")

```

#get a clean, readable table
```{r}
long_covid_kwic_df <- as.data.frame(long_covid_kwic_results)
names(long_covid_kwic_df)
```
```{r}
view(long_covid_kwic_df)
```

#SUMMARY OF FINDINGS
#Overall, I found my findings interesting. I put 12 different keywords in search: broadly "long COVID" to understand how the word is being used in context within article texts, some specific symptoms of long COVID, and then words like "quality of life", "mental health", "not real" to try and understand how long COVID is being framed or position in relation to mental health or quality-of-life related issues. I chose these keywords because I see a critique of the psychologization of long COVID in the community, and wanted to see if I can quickly catch any evidence of media contribution to that in the keyword search. I also included some research-focused keywords to try and see how research on long COVID was being framed. 
#Some interesting findings regarding the framing of "long COVID" in context of the article texts is that it is used in more descriptive scenarios: articles describing features or symptoms of long COVID, indicated by the keyword being followed by "heart disease, parkinson's", etc. But also, I saw a few times that long COVID was also discussed as something to worry about even if acute COVID-19 infection is not severed. There were a few different sentences across the articles explaining that risk of long COVID continues to be a problem irrespective or prevalence or severity of acute COVID-19. 
#For my hypothesis about media framing long COVID as a psychological rather than physiological condition, I didnt'really see much evidence of that. First of all, not many articles came up that used the term "mental health" or "not real". I wonder if this is just because of what articles were selected into the corpus or reflecting current standards in reporting on long COVID. It is probably not possible to say. 
#For my keyword search on "chronic fatigue", one thing that I found interesting was that there was a comparison between long COVID and other conditions like fibromyalgia or ME/CFS. This is complicated. From my experiences being embedded in the community, sometimes there are points of alignment, shared struggles. Many of these communities also experience the stigma of their symptoms being attributed to psychological causes, and thus not being able to access healthcare that actually alleviates their symptoms. Regardless, there were very few articles on this, and I am not able to make claims about media framing of these issues. 
#Overall, I did think this was a helpful way to get more familiar with my data, and understand how some specific keywords were being discussed in context. I think it is just hard to be comprehensive with a key word search, because even if a construct is talked about, I might not be using all the keywords needed to actually get at it.
